ABOUT US

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor https://www.linkedin.com/in/brettaylor/ and Clay Bavor https://www.linkedin.com/in/claybavor/. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Architect Sierra's most complex deals: Lead our largest multi-BU, multi-geo opportunities, designing sophisticated deal structures and managing risk with precision and conviction.

 - Operate as part of the customer's team: Hold trusted relationships across the customer C-suite and working teams.

 - Engage at the founder level: Be trusted to regularly engage and manage Sierra's co-founders in front of customers, pitching with co-founder-like conviction and expertise.

 - Bring precision to everything: Operate with exacting craft in messaging, positioning, and timing across every interaction.

 - Shape strategy: Influence how Sierra approaches its most important accounts and set the standard for the broader sales org.

 - Operate as an AI-native seller: Leverage AI tools across the full sales cycle- account research, personalized outreach, call summarization, pipeline forecasting, and deal execution- to automate low-value tasks and reinvest that time into high-value customer relationships, while continuously adopting and experimenting with new tools to work faster and smarter than traditional methods allow.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 10-12+ years of enterprise/strategic sales experience, owning the largest and most complex accounts.

 - Demonstrated success closing multi-million-dollar, multi-stakeholder deals spanning business units and geographies.

 - Experience managing a $1M+ quota and running end-to-end complex 6- and 7-figure ACV deals.

 - Deep, sustained C-suite relationships and the gravitas to be treated as a peer by executive buyers.

 - Mastery of complex deal structuring, risk navigation, and pricing.

 - Exceptional executive communication and a reputation for precision and trust.


EVEN BETTER...

 - Deep familiarity with the AI landscape and the ability to speak credibly to technical and business stakeholders alike.

 - Experience operating alongside founders/executives in front of strategic customers.

 - Experience building GTM strategies: Building sales teams and sales motions from scratch, or from early stage growth.


OUR VALUES

 - Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

 - Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

 - Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

 - Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 - Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.


WHAT WE OFFER

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

 - Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 - Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life insurance and disability benefits

 - Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 - Parental leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

 - Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 - Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


BE YOU, WITH US

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

The estimator must instill confidence in the customer and provide clear expectations. The estimator must understand the effect of collision to a vehicle and highlight damages. The detailed estimate must include factory researched repair specifications and adhere to shop policies and insurer guidelines where applicable.

 Set reasonable expectations for the customer, and educate them on the repair process 
 Have thorough understanding of estimating software, required to process estimates. 
 Locating assignments from insurers and understanding the requirements. Understanding terms on assignment – LOU-Loss of use, WP- With prejudice, 43endorsement, betterment, deductible.

 Determine if a vehicle is drivable or non-drivable 
 Determine if a vehicle requires disassembly for an accurate estimate.

Are you a Machine Learning practitioner who is technically deep and commercially sharp? 

If so, this might be the role for you! We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Applied Machine Learning (ML) to join our growing Data Science team.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn't like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That's why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

We help employees grow professionally; we have a ton of onboarding resources, tutorials, hackathons and buddies to support learnings and provide opportunities to innovate. We have a range of experience levels on teams which allows for mentor/mentee opportunities. Leaders at Jobber work with empathy and support employees to build healthy work-life harmony. Bring your dedication and passion to this job to fulfill your goals.


The team:


Similar to how Jobber empowers small businesses with the tools and insights they need to succeed, the Strategy and Analytics Department ensures our people at Jobber have the tooling, data insights, and strategic direction to excel in our shared mission. We turn data into actionable insights, and critical business needs into impactful software, working with multiple teams and departments across the company. Strategy & Analytics serves as a central hub that drives business outcomes in all corners of Jobber's ecosystem.

Within that department, Data Science is the predictive and prescriptive arm. We're a small, hungry team with an outsized footprint. We work in two-week sprints, demo to the whole department, and expect each other to bring a point of view rather than a ticket.

SignalGraph is our next major project: a company-wide metric graph that connects organizational activity and outcomes so teams can trace metric movement to root causes, investigate faster, and make better decisions.


The role:

Reporting to the Manager, Data Science, the Staff Data Scientist, Applied Machine Learning will own models and systems for automated decisioning. You will train and evaluate models using techniques such as graph representation learning, transformer architectures, and ranking, and engineer them to serve reliably in real time and at scale inside Jobber's product.



This is a senior individual contributor role with strong architectural scope. You'll be the person who decides how ML systems at Jobber are built, evaluated, and trusted and you'll be doing it against a dataset most companies our size don't have: high-velocity SaaS event data, scheduling data, and payments data across hundreds of thousands of service professionals and millions of their clients, plus a rich body of unstructured sales and support text.


The Staff Data Scientist, Applied Machine Learning will:


 - Continue building, improving, and maintaining SignalGraph: evolve metric-family contracts, keep segment and causal-edge catalogs trustworthy, operate the Neo4j and series-refresh pipeline, and strengthen investigation diagnostics so teams can trace metric changes to root causes and make faster decisions from governed evidence..
   

 - Design, build, and evaluate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems on top of that graph. You’ll own retrieval quality, context management, and the evaluation harness that proves the system is actually right, not just fluent.
   

 - Own production ML end-to-end: training pipelines, real-time serving, monitoring, drift detection, and retraining. When a model is live, its uptime, latency, and accuracy are yours.
   

 - Establish systematic evaluation and regression testing as a standard for the team — so model and LLM system quality is measured and defended over time rather than assessed once at launch.
   

 - Set the technical bar and multiply the team: drive MLOps and ML engineering standards, shape our feature store and platform roadmap, review peers' work, and mentor other scientists on graph and deep learning methods.
   

 - Partner directly with senior leadership. Much of what you build will be used by Senior Leaders, Customer Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Product to make decisions against Jobber's North Star goals. You'll present your own work, defend your assumptions, and help cross-functional partners reframe how they approach a problem.
   

 - Stay current, and bring it back. We expect this role to be the most informed person at Jobber on developments in AI/ML methodologically, not just as a consumer of tools, and to translate that into shipped capability.


To be successful, you should have:


 - Production ML experience, end-to-end. You've trained, deployed, served, and maintained models that acted on real users (not just scored offline) You've learned the hard lessons about retraining, drift, and technical debt that come with it.
   

 - A strong statistics foundation. You can reason about bias and variance, justify a loss function, and tell signal from noise without hand-waving.
   

 - Expert SQL and production-grade Python skills. 
   

 - Depth in modern ML methods: Deep learning and neural architectures, transformers/BERT-family models, RNN/CNN, ranking, and representation learning, with hands-on experience applying LLMs in production systems, including RAG and context management.
   

 - Experience designing for the real cost of being wrong. You've built or tuned custom and asymmetric loss functions where a miss in one direction is far more expensive than the other, and you can explain the business reasoning behind the choice.
   

 - Experience with large data in production environments and the platforms that support it. ML/AI platforms such as Snowflake, orchestration with Apache Airflow, and cloud infrastructure (AWS strongly preferred; GCP or Azure equivalent considered).
   

 - Strong communication and stakeholder alignment skills. This team's work only lands if everyone shares the same understanding of what the data means. You can take a room of technical and non-technical partners from confusion to alignment, present uncertainty honestly, and influence without authority.
   

 - Ownership of quality over shipping speed alone. You want to know why something works and how to make it better. You don't accept a model's current performance as its ceiling, and you don't outsource your understanding of your own code to an AI assistant.


It would be nice if you had:


 - Graph experience: Graph theory, graph neural networks, knowledge graphs, or graph databases such as Neo4j. Rare, and the single most valuable thing you could bring to this role.
   

 - A software engineering background: Services and model serving (REST/gRPC), Docker/Kubernetes, CI/CD, feature stores.
   

 - Experience with Snowflake, including Snowpark and Snowpark Container Services, or a comparable path from warehouse to deployed model.

 - Experience building LLM evaluation infrastructure, safety layers, or LLMOps for customer-facing AI.
   

 - Exposure to risk, fraud, or fintech modelling, or to recommendation and ranking systems at scale.

Compensation:

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!



What you can expect from Jobber:

Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team 
 The Link Partnerships team sources, develops, and manages relationships with the payments ecosystem partners that power Link, Stripe's consumer wallet. Our team drives the growth and utility of Link by building partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, crypto providers, and emerging commerce platforms. We execute on high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that expand Link's acceptance, improve performance, and enable new payment experiences—including agentic commerce. These partnerships have a significant impact on Stripe and the products used by millions of our users.
 What you’ll do 
 We're looking for a Partner Development Manager who builds and manages Link's payments partnerships with card networks, card issuers, local payment method providers, and crypto and stablecoin providers. You'll own the strategy and execution of partnerships that expand Link's payment capabilities, improve transaction performance, and position Link as the default payments layer for agentic commerce. You'll negotiate commercial agreements, drive technical integrations, and shape Link's payments roadmap in collaboration with these partners. As part of these efforts, you'll collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Risk, and others. You'll also lead relationship management and partner closely with external partners' executive leadership.
 Responsibilities 
 Define and execute Link's payments partnership strategy across card networks, card issuers, local payment methods, and crypto and stablecoins
 Negotiate and manage commercial agreements with payment partners that expand Link's acceptance footprint, improve authorization rates, and unlock new payment capabilities
 Develop a deep understanding of the card network and issuer landscape—including scheme rules, tokenization frameworks, authentication protocols, and competitive dynamics—to inform partnership strategy
 Drive partnerships that enable Link to serve as the payments layer for agentic commerce, working with networks and issuers to establish rules, liability frameworks, and technical standards for agent-initiated transactions
 Gather inputs from and coordinate with internal cross-functional stakeholders (including product, risk, compliance, engineering, and security) to drive creation and execution of partner strategy including our global LPM roadmap
 Work closely with Product and Engineering to define requirements and shape Link's payments product roadmap based on partner capabilities and market opportunities
 Identify partner stakeholders who will champion Stripe, educate them about Link's value proposition, and build alignment between Stripe and our partners' executive teams
 Identify and effectively analyze new partnership opportunities, ultimately making recommendations to relevant decision makers and cross-functional stakeholders
 Exhibit an operationally focused mindset, with an ability to lead teams through complex relationship management activities by setting a clear vision and running tight processes
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 
 You're a skilled dealmaker and a strategist by nature. You understand how to work closely with Product and Engineering teams and can formulate partner strategies that drive tangible and measurable results. You're energized by the intersection of payments infrastructure and emerging commerce models, and you see the opportunity to define how payments work in an agentic world. 
 Minimum requirements 
 10+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, corporate development, or related field
 5+ years of experience in or working closely with card networks, card issuers, digital wallets, or payments infrastructure providers
 3+ years of experience negotiating commercial deals with partners, including scaling such deals across multiple partners
 Strong communication skills, in both verbal and written form, and ability to influence stakeholders across a wide variety of functions, including at executive levels
 Technical acumen, especially an ability to understand product strategy and use this understanding to define requirements for scaling products through partnerships
 Experience developing partnership strategies and identifying, sourcing, and analyzing new partnership opportunities in greenfield segments
 Strong agency, can handle ambiguity in a fast-moving organization, and thrives on a high level of autonomy and responsibility
 Preferred qualifications 
 Familiarity with card scheme rules, tokenization (network tokens, device tokens), authentication frameworks (3DS, SCA), and issuer-side authorization optimization
 Experience with emerging payment models such as agentic commerce, embedded payments, or programmable payment flows
 Experience building a new partnership category or vertical from zero—defining the strategy, establishing first partnerships, and scaling the program

 Side est un fournisseur mondial de services et de développement de jeux vidéo. Nous offrons des services techniques et créatifs à plusieurs des plus grands développeurs et studios au monde. Fondée au Japon en 1994, PTW est devenue une force mondiale dans l’industrie du jeu vidéo, avec plus de 40 studios dans 14 pays et des bureaux en Amérique du Nord, en Europe, en Amérique du Sud et en Asie. Nos services de premier plan comprennent la production artistique, le développement de jeux, l’assurance qualité, le soutien aux joueurs, la gestion de communauté, la localisation, l’assurance qualité de la localisation, la production audio et la collecte de données. La famille de marques Side comprend Ghostpunch Games et 1518 Studios. Pour en savoir plus, visitez https://www.side.inc/ 
 L’occasion 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne pour occuper le poste de gestionnaire des finances à Montréal, au Québec. Cette personne sera responsable de la gestion financière de nos studios de livraison basés aux États-Unis et prendra en charge l’ensemble du processus de clôture mensuelle. En plus d’assurer l’exactitude de la clôture mensuelle et des rapports financiers, la personne titulaire du poste agira comme partenaire d’affaires auprès des directeurs de studio. Le rôle comprend la tenue de livres, la clôture mensuelle, la préparation des états financiers, la production et l’analyse de rapports financiers et de gestion, ainsi que la collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe des finances situés dans différents emplacements. 
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Clôture mensuelle et production de rapports financiers 
 Diriger les activités quotidiennes de clôture mensuelle, y compris la facturation aux clients, les paiements aux fournisseurs, les rapprochements bancaires et les rapprochements de comptes. 
 Préparer et réviser les écritures de journal, les comptes du bilan, la trésorerie, les comptes clients, les comptes fournisseurs et les transactions intersociétés. 
 Analyser les écarts, résoudre les divergences et veiller à ce que les rapports soient produits avec exactitude et dans les délais. 
 Coordonner la production mensuelle de rapports à la société mère japonaise dans les délais requis et soutenir le processus de consolidation aux États-Unis. 
 Grand livre, immobilisations et états financiers 
 Tenir à jour le grand livre dans Microsoft Dynamics 365 et veiller à ce que les données financières soient exactes et adéquatement appuyées. 
 Gérer la comptabilisation des immobilisations, y compris les calendriers d’amortissement, les écritures de journal, les acquisitions, les cessions et les dépréciations. 
 Préparer les états des résultats, les bilans et les états des flux de trésorerie conformément aux normes comptables applicables. 
 Maintenir la documentation à l’appui des écritures financières, des rapports et de la préparation aux audits. 
 Conformité, contrôles et soutien aux audits 
 Assurer la conformité aux contrôles internes, aux politiques de l’entreprise ainsi qu’aux exigences locales, étatiques, fédérales et comptables applicables. 
 Soutenir la production des déclarations réglementaires dans les délais requis et maintenir des dossiers exacts pour les dépôts obligatoires. 
 Fournir la documentation et les explications nécessaires aux demandes d’audit interne et externe. 
 Examiner les données de paie afin d’en assurer l’exactitude relativement à la rémunération, aux retenues, aux calculs fiscaux et à la conformité aux politiques. 
 Partenariat d’affaires et collaboration interfonctionnelle

 Coordonner avec la trésorerie du groupe la prévision de trésorerie hebdomadaire et mensuelle. 
 Amélioration des processus et excellence opérationnelle 
 Repérer les occasions d’améliorer le processus de clôture mensuelle, l’exactitude des rapports et l’ensemble des flux de travail financiers. 
 Recommander et mettre en œuvre des pratiques exemplaires qui améliorent la cohérence, l’efficacité et la gestion des échéances.

 Baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe, et/ou titre de comptable professionnel agréé, comme CPA canadien, CPA américain ou équivalent, ou être en voie d’obtenir une qualification pertinente. 
 Maîtrise des logiciels de comptabilité et des systèmes de gestion intégrés; une expérience avec Microsoft Dynamics 365 est un atout. 
 Expérience importante en comptabilité complète, idéalement au sein d’une petite ou moyenne entreprise. 
 Solide connaissance des normes comptables, comme les PCGR ou les IFRS. 
 Excellentes compétences organisationnelles, grand souci du détail et capacité à respecter des échéances serrées. 
 Esprit analytique et solides compétences en résolution de problèmes. 
 Maîtrise intermédiaire ou avancée de Microsoft Office, notamment Excel, PowerPoint et Word, avec une expertise particulière dans Excel. 
 Benefits

 Chez Side, vous vous joindrez à une équipe mondiale passionnée par les jeux vidéo, la technologie et les gens. Vous aurez l’occasion d’avoir une incidence concrète sur les opérations financières de nos studios américains en soutenant la production de rapports exacts, en améliorant les processus de clôture mensuelle et en collaborant avec les équipes des studios et des finances dans nos emplacements à l’échelle mondiale.
 About Us 
 Side is a global video game development and services provider, providing technical and creative services to many of the largest developers and studios around the world. Founded in Japan in 1994, PTW has grown to become a global force in the gaming industry, with over 40 studios in 14 countries worldwide and offices across North America, Europe, South America, and Asia.  The Opportunity

 What You Will Do: 
 Monthly Close and Financial Reporting 
 Lead day-to-day monthly close activities, including customer billing, supplier payments, bank reconciliations, and account reconciliations.

 Process Improvement and Operational Excellence 
 Identify opportunities to improve the monthly close process, reporting accuracy, and overall finance workflows. 
 Recommend and implement best practices that improve consistency, efficiency, and deadline management. 
 Strengthen documentation, controls, and communication across finance, studio operations, and corporate stakeholders. 
 What We Are Looking For 
 Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, and/or Qualified Accountant (Canadian CA/CPAUS CPA or equivalent)/actively pursuing qualification. 
 Proficiency in accounting software and ERP systems (experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 is a plus). 
 Significant end-to-end accounting experience within a small to midsized company is preferred 
 Strong knowledge of accounting standards such as GAAP or IFRS. 
 Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to meet tight deadlines. 
 Analytical mindset with strong problem-solving skills. 
 Intermediate or above of MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word), Excel in particular. 
 Why Join Side 
 At Side, you'll join a global team passionate about games, technology, and people. You'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the financial operations of our US studios by supporting accurate reporting, improving monthly close processes, and partnering with studio and finance teams across our global locations.

The Freight & Logistics Planner is responsible for keeping shipments moving at the best cost and service level. The role analyzes freight spend, carrier performance and shipping patterns. It turns those findings into recommendations on routing, mode selection, carrier sourcing and cost reduction, and works closely with carriers, warehouse teams, procurement and finance.
 The Freight and Logistics Planner plays an integral role in our Customer Experience and ensures our Customers receive exceptional service throughout the flow of order processing, as well as ensuring problems with order flow are expertly resolved. 
 In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with Tayco’s motivated and engaging team, enjoy Tayco’s fantastic culture which has won us our Great Place to Work certification, as well as be an important part of our exciting growth plans.
 This posting is for an existing vacancy.
 Responsibilities: 
 Load planning and scheduling: Plan inbound and outbound shipments and build loads that make the best use of trailer and container space. 
 Carrier booking: Tender loads to contracted carriers or brokers, choose the right mode (FTL, LTL, intermodal, or air) and confirm capacity.
 Shipment tracking: Monitor freight in transit and give customers and internal teams proactive updates on delays or exceptions. Work with CER and Scheduling when customer has a must arrive date.
 Issue resolution: Handle missed pickups, delays, damages, refused deliveries and re-routing, and file claims when needed. Minimize freight claims and work with the freight partners to find the root cause. File freight claims on time with all freight carriers.
 Documentation: Prepare and check bills of lading, packing lists, commercial invoices and customs paperwork. Coordinate with customs brokers on cross-border shipments.
 Warehouse coordination: Line up dock schedules, staffing needs and order readiness with the warehouse so loads ship on time.
 Cost control: Choose cost-effective routes and carriers, consolidate shipments where possible and keep accessorial charges (detention, redelivery, storage) to a minimum. Reduce freight cost on an ongoing basis established in the business plan, annualized savings on the freight costs (Gross sales v/s freight costs). 
 Systems: Keep shipment data, rates and appointments accurate in the ERP.
 Performance tracking: Report on carrier on-time performance, OTIF and shipping costs, and suggest process improvements. 
 Compliance: Make sure shipments follow DOT and Transport Canada rules, hours-of-service limits, dangerous goods/hazmat rules and customs regulations.
 Sourcing and qualification: Find new carriers and service providers when you need more capacity, new lanes or backup options. Collect carrier profiles covering equipment types, service areas, fleet size, specialties (reefer, flatbed, hazmat, cross-border) and references. Screen carriers against company criteria such as years in business, safety record, financial stability and capacity.
 We are seeking passionate candidates who possess the following experience and competencies: 
 Post-secondary diploma or degree in supply chain, logistics or business, or equivalent experience.
 3-5 years of experience in transportation planning, dispatch or freight coordination
 Knowledge of freight modes, Incoterms and shipping documentation
 Strong Excel skills and comfort working in a TMS and ERP
 Able to juggle priorities and make quick decisions under pressure
 Clear, professional communication with carriers and customers
 This position is also required to wear PPE (safety shoes, safety glasses, and hi-visibility vest) when in the plant / warehouse.

We are seeking a strategic, collaborative and product-minded leader to join our team as Assistant Vice President (AVP), Enterprise Digital Capabilities. This role is a key leader in Manulife's multi-year transformation to modernize and converge our digital ecosystem across Canada, the US, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.
At the heart of this role is a simple objective: identify what is common across our digital experiences, build it once as an enterprise capability, and enable markets and segments to reuse and extend it to accelerate their own digital roadmaps.
Manulife has established a strong portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities that support our Digital Storefront transformation and broader unification ambitions. The next opportunity is to expand and scale this portfolio to accelerate the unification strategies and roadmaps of our segments and advance One Manulife experiences across the enterprise. The AVP will lead this evolution – working across segments to identify where common capabilities can create the greatest incremental value, bringing together requirements to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise reuse, defining adoption and rollout strategies, and establishing a federated model where capabilities can be developed globally or contributed by segments and scaled for broader enterprise benefit.
The AVP will own the strategy and evolution of this portfolio — identifying new opportunities for reuse, prioritizing investment, establishing strong product management disciplines, driving adoption, optimizing existing capabilities and ensuring that each enterprise investment continues to deliver measurable value.
A critical part of the role is leading the Common Capability Collective, bringing together digital and product leaders from across the enterprise to identify common needs, align roadmaps, determine where enterprise investment can eliminate duplication and accelerate delivery, and create a shared view of capability priorities.
This is an enablement role, not ownership of individual market or segment experiences. The AVP will partner closely with Digital Storefront and segment digital leaders to understand their roadmaps and determine how enterprise capabilities can help them deliver faster, with greater quality, consistency and efficiency.
The AVP will operate in a two-in-a-box partnership with a complementary Global Technology leader, jointly shaping the business and technology evolution of enterprise digital capabilities. Together, they will ensure capabilities are scalable, secure, reusable, well-integrated and designed for long-term enterprise value.
 Position Responsibilities 
 Enterprise Capability Strategy & Portfolio 
 Own the strategy, roadmap and ongoing evolution of Manulife's portfolio of reusable enterprise digital capabilities.
 Establish a clear view of the capabilities required to support digital convergence across markets, segments and channels.
 Continuously identify common business and customer needs that can be solved once and reused across the enterprise.
 Assess existing segment capabilities for opportunities to scale them globally rather than rebuilding equivalent solutions.
 Prioritize enterprise investment based on customer value, segment demand, reuse potential, strategic alignment and economic benefit.
 Maintain a multi-year capability roadmap aligned to Digital Storefront, segment roadmaps and Manulife's broader digital strategy.
 Ensure the portfolio remains focused and sustainable by rationalizing overlapping capabilities, technology and licenses where appropriate.
 Common Capability Collective & Federated Leadership 
 Lead the Common Capability Collective, bringing together Digital Storefront and product leaders from across the enterprise to jointly shape capability priorities and investment.
 Create transparency across segment roadmaps to identify shared needs, opportunities for reuse and potential duplication before investment occurs.
 Establish a federated model that enables capabilities to originate within segments where appropriate and subsequently evolve into reusable enterprise capabilities.
 Build alignment around enterprise standards and shared capabilities while preserving segment accountability for their own customer experiences and business outcomes.
 Create clear decision rights, funding principles, ownership models and governance for the creation and evolution of common capabilities.
 Product Management & Capability Evolution 
 Establish strong product management disciplines across the enterprise capability portfolio, including product vision, roadmaps, adoption, performance measurement and lifecycle management.
 Ensure every capability has clear customer and business outcomes, ownership, success measures and an evolution roadmap.
 Use segment feedback, performance data and emerging customer needs to continuously improve capabilities.
 Drive adoption and reuse across markets and segments, ensuring enterprise investments translate into meaningful acceleration of local roadmaps.
 Ensure capabilities are designed for extensibility so segments can meet differentiated market needs without unnecessarily duplicating core functionality.
 Manage capabilities through their full lifecycle, including investment, enhancement, optimization, consolidation and retirement.
 AI Enablement & Optimization

 Identify opportunities to embed AI directly into capabilities to improve customer experiences, decisioning, personalization and digital effectiveness.
 Apply AI and automation across the capability lifecycle to accelerate development, testing, implementation, operations and ongoing optimization.

 Define business requirements and product priorities while partnering with Technology on architecture, engineering, security, scalability and technical lifecycle management.
 Ensure enterprise capabilities are designed to integrate effectively across Manulife's digital ecosystem and can be consumed by multiple platforms, markets and channels.
 Promote API-enabled, modular and reusable approaches that reduce point-to-point solutions and technology duplication.
 Ensure platform and technology decisions support long-term reuse, interoperability and enterprise scale.
 Business Value & Benefits Realization 
 Establish a clear value proposition and business case for enterprise digital capabilities and the overall portfolio.
 Quantify and track the value generated through reuse, including delivery acceleration, avoided duplicate investment, license consolidation, operational efficiency, improved customer experience and reduced ongoing support costs.
 Demonstrate how building once and reusing at scale compounds speed, quality and efficiency with every additional implementation.
 Partner with Global Marketing Strategy, FP&A, Technology and segment teams to track expected and realized benefits.
 Use adoption, utilization, performance and financial data to inform ongoing investment and portfolio decisions.
 Adoption & Enterprise Enablement 
 Partner with segment digital leaders to understand upcoming priorities and proactively identify enterprise capabilities that can accelerate their roadmaps.
 Establish clear onboarding, documentation, implementation patterns and support models that make enterprise capabilities easy for teams to adopt.

Success in this role means Manulife increasingly builds once and benefits many times.
Segments are able to deliver their digital roadmaps faster because proven enterprise capabilities are readily available rather than repeatedly designed, procured and built. Capabilities originating in one part of Manulife can be scaled for the benefit of others. Duplicate technology and investment decline. Adoption and reuse increase.  About Our Approach: 
 We believe apparent correctness is not enough: code must respect underlying concepts, with types and named algorithms directly describing the domain. Great code is correct-by-construction, with any remaining uncertainties ruled-out by a suite of unit tests. Furthermore, great design does not happen by accident: it requires clear principles, and the willingness to defend and refine them through spirited deliberation. We strive to write pure, compositional code, with any inevitable impure code tamed by a rigid stratification of effects. To this end, we write TypeScript in a functional programming style. We have an enduring commitment to satisfy the needs of our rapidly growing business, understanding that great code is essential for our continued growth and success. We place a strong emphasis on domain modelling and understanding the nature of the problems that we are solving and will spend considerable time engaged with research and experimental development. We have regular presentations, where engineers talk about whatever excites them, with previous topics including programming language theory, Master's Thesis presentations, World of Warcraft addons, and the philosophy of Machine Learning.

 You will build and maintain both new projects and existing systems in a team environment, ensuring stability and long-term maintainability. 
 You will own projects from start to finish, learn and model the associated domain, specify the implementation design, and execute in accordance with your plan. 
 You will communicate progress and coordinate release efforts.

About the Role

We are seeking an exceptional Principal Product Manager to build the HTS API Marketplace — the commercial and developer-facing layer through which enterprise partners access Hopper's lodging and cars capabilities.

This is a true 0-to-1 role. You will be the person who defines what it is: how capabilities are packaged and priced, how partners discover and integrate them, and how the marketplace evolves as a platform business. The underlying technical capabilities — connectivity orchestration, pricing and sort, content mapping, the extranet — are owned by dedicated capability teams. Your job is to work closely with those PMs to understand, package, and commercially expose those capabilities as coherent, enterprise-grade API products.

We expect this PM to move fast and build scrappily. You should be comfortable using AI tools and vibe coding to prototype workflows, mock APIs, and test partner experiences before handing off to engineering. The best candidate will reach for a prototype before a PRD.

You will partner with Engineering, Data Science, Commercial, Finance, and Supply — and coordinate tightly with other PMs across the organization — to bring the marketplace from concept to a revenue-generating platform.



This is a fully remote role.




WHAT WOULD YOUR DAY-TO-DAY LOOK LIKE:

 - Define what the HTS API Marketplace is: how capabilities are structured, packaged, and priced across a portfolio spanning HTS Connect, Search Polygons, Autocomplete, Ranking, Content & Property Mapping, Room Mapping, Deduplication/Auction, Pricing, Extranet, Taxes, and Custom Deals Engine.

 - Coordinate with capability PMs — who own the underlying technical systems — to understand each capability's roadmap, constraints, and customization surface, and translate that into externally-consumable API products.

 - Own the commercial model for the marketplace: platform vs. variable fee decisions, take rate structure per capability, enterprise packaging, and the custom deals framework for large partners with differentiated customer segments.

 - Build the developer and partner experience from scratch: API specifications, partner onboarding flows, documentation standards, sandbox environments, and integration tooling that minimizes time-to-first-value.

 - Use AI tools and rapid prototyping to test ideas quickly — mock API responses, prototype partner portals, simulate pricing and ranking configurations — before committing engineering resources.

 - Establish the go-to-market motion for the marketplace: work with Commercial to identify the right partners for each capability, sequence launches, and define what a successful commercial rollout looks like.

 - Own the marketplace revenue P&L: model and track GBV, take rate, and per-capability unit economics in partnership with Finance.
   


AN IDEAL CANDIDATE HAS:

 - 7+ years of Product Management experience, with at least one 0-to-1 product you built from concept to commercial launch.

 - Demonstrated experience building developer-facing or B2B marketplace products, including ownership of API product design, developer experience, and commercial packaging for enterprise customers.

 - AI-native working style: you use LLMs and vibe coding as first-line tools for prototyping, not as novelties. You have built working demos, mockups, or proof-of-concepts using AI before handing work to engineering.

 - Strong understanding of marketplace economics: take rates, supply-side incentives, demand-side optimization, and the design of platform vs. variable commercial models.

 - Ability to coordinate effectively across multiple product teams — you can synthesize roadmaps, surface dependencies, and drive cross-team alignment without owning the underlying engineering.

 - Experience working with external enterprise partners: translating commercial needs into product requirements and managing partner expectations through multi-phase rollouts.

 - Strong fluency with SQL and large-scale transactional or operational datasets.

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to write crisp API and product documentation.

Bonus:

 - Experience in travel commerce (lodging, cars, flights) or adjacent industries such as fintech, ads, or marketplace infrastructure.

 - Background in connectivity, distribution, or supplier technology (GDS, channel managers, OTA APIs).

 - Prior experience in Engineering, Data Science, or a technical role.

 - Familiarity with auction or deduplication mechanics, dynamic pricing systems, or recommendation and ranking models.
   


PERKS & BENEFITS OF WORKING WITH US:

 - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages.

 - Hopper covers 100% of the premiums for group insurance plan.

About the Role
 You will be the person who makes our AI better at selling. You will read its conversations, notice what is working and what is not, and change the instructions it follows so the next thousand conversations go better.
 You do not need to know everything on day one. We will teach you our tools, our playbooks and how to write and test prompts. What we cannot teach is the instinct for conversations, a feel for sales, and the curiosity to dig into the data and ask why.
 What You'll Do
 Review AI-drafted text messages each day, and approve, edit or rewrite them before they send.
 Spot patterns across conversations, such as an opener that gets replies but no orders, and figure out the cause.
 Update each brand's prompts and playbook to fix problems at the source, then test the change before it goes live.
 Respond to brand requests and turn them into playbook updates.
 Help launch new brands: deep research on their brand, write the persona and opening messages, and check that offers work.
 Run and track A/B tests, and report what won. 
 You read people well. From one text you can tell whether a shopper is ready to buy, has a question, or is done, and you reply the way a real person would.
 You have sales instinct. You answer an objection and then ask for the sale, without arguing or pushing the customer away.
 You are curious about data. You can open a table of conversations and ask the right questions: how many, compared to what, at which brand, since when. You notice when a number looks off and go find out why.
 You fix the cause, not the symptom. When the AI says something wrong, you look for the reason (a missing fact, a vague rule, two rules that conflict) and fix the instruction so it does not happen again.
 You are comfortable with AI tools. You use ChatGPT, Claude or similar tools regularly and understand that how you ask shapes what you get back.
 You are online. These are live conversations. You are responsive during working hours and quick to pick things up in Slack.

 Familiarity with Shopify, Klaviyo, Postscript or similar tools.
 Spreadsheet skills, or basic SQL.
 Something you have built or automated with AI on your own.
 What We'll Teach You
 Our console, approval queue and playbook system.
 How to write, test and ship prompt changes.
 Shopify basics, discount codes and how they combine.
 How we run and read A/B tests.

 About this position 
 As a Senior Data Platform Engineer at Later, you'll own the foundation our data ecosystem runs on. You'll design, build, and evolve the infrastructure, backend services, and platform capabilities that move data from source to decision, and that help engineers, analysts, and data scientists do their best work.
 This is a data engineering role with a platform mindset. Our analytics platform runs on GCP and BigQuery, and our operational databases live in AWS. You'll shape how data moves between them, modernize what we have, and get our data ready for the AI-powered products we're building. You'll treat the platform as a product and the teams who depend on it as your customers.
 This role is for someone who likes building the system more than the individual report or model. It isn't a traditional ETL/ELT role focused on SQL, dashboards, and pipeline maintenance, and it isn't an ML engineering or data science role. You'll build the data foundation that makes AI work, and other teams will build on top of it.
 What you'll be doing 
 Build, own, and evolve the data platform 
 Design and own scalable infrastructure across ingestion, orchestration, storage, transformation, and consumption, including our BigQuery warehouse and lakehouse. Make architectural decisions, explain the tradeoffs, and modernize the parts that have outgrown their original design.
 Build reliable batch and real-time pipelines and dbt transformation layers. Evolve our orchestration (GCP-native tools plus our custom orchestrator) and shape our ingestion strategy, including how we evaluate Fivetran against custom connectors.
 Spot weaknesses in the platform and drive the fixes. Mentor other engineers and raise the technical bar.
 Engineer backend systems and keep them reliable 
 Build the APIs, services, and integrations that move data in and out of the platform, including secure, cost-aware data movement between GCP and AWS. Manage infrastructure as code and automate deployment with CI/CD.
 Build observability, data quality checks, and access controls, and optimize performance and cost. Create reusable tooling and standards that make the right way the easy way.
 Build the foundation for AI 
 Make trusted company data accessible for analytics, machine learning, and AI applications, including LLMs and AI agents. Invest in data quality, metadata, lineage, governance, and freshness.
 Design the platform to absorb new AI use cases without major rework, and partner with AI/ML, product, and engineering teams on what they need.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience 
 6+ years in data engineering, backend engineering, or platform engineering, with a track record of owning production data systems at scale and improving their reliability, performance, and cost.
 Strong backend programming skills (Python or similar), solid SQL, and experience with dbt or a similar transformation framework.
 Hands-on cloud experience, ideally GCP and BigQuery, and comfort working across more than one cloud.
 Experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and workflow orchestration.
 Experience with batch and streaming architectures, and a working understanding of security, access control, and data governance.
 The judgment to make architectural decisions and explain the tradeoffs to technical and non-technical partners.
 Nice to have 
 Kubernetes, and experience migrating or redesigning orchestration systems.
 Managed ingestion tools like Fivetran.
 Experience building internal platforms or tooling that other engineers adopt.
 Data foundations for AI, such as vector stores, feature pipelines, or governed LLM access.
